title: New Flowchart Shapes (with new syntax)
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary
This pull request introduces several new flowchart shapes along with their test, updates to the configuration files, and improvements to the documentation.

**The most important changes include a guide for other contributors on how to add a new custom shape for flowcharts.
### New Tests and Configurations:

* [`cypress/integration/rendering/flowchart-v2.spec.js`](diffhunk://#diff-c496530fa45816d603f73358c33be87869deb0563f89b32c889507f94e26d1a9R1055-R1077): Added a test to render self-loops in flowcharts.
* [`cypress/integration/rendering/newShapes.spec.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-8f97593c2d6ddb3ca2a04b273aca08f4bbe6f06c7adea9233854231b421f1885R1-R129): Introduced comprehensive tests for new shapes, including various looks, directions, labels, and styles.
* [`cypress/integration/rendering/oldShapes.spec.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-869e7b6ef5a3878a28e5fa33083db4f1151c08c486ff165be615531b452db5e0R1-R101): Added tests for existing shapes with different looks and directions.

### Configuration Updates:

* [`.cspell/cspell.config.yaml`](diffhunk://#diff-5f297dd85a718d0aac9b7159811a26178f421e331f28df6dfe60949572de2afbR31-R33): Added new words to the dictionary definitions.

### Documentation Enhancements:

* [`docs/adding_new_shape/Readme.md`](diffhunk://#diff-fceaf55c22d4a4736bd2a9e93fd039918da625cad4288f4218234964748a2f98R1-R222): Added detailed documentation on the available utilities for creating new shapes, instructions for adding new shapes, and information on running Cypress tests.

These changes collectively enhance the robustness of the flowchart rendering capabilities and provide clear guidelines for extending the shape library.

comments.body: We're embedding roughjs very deeply into a lot of places. Very tight coupling, which will be really hard to change later.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags tight coupling with roughjs as a concern that should be addressed to allow easier future changes.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
These shapes don't follow the kebab-case convention. 

Also, why did we choose kebab-case? Look is camelCase `handDrawn`. Shouldn't we be consistent?
comments.label_reasoning: Flags that shapes don't follow the project's kebab-case naming convention and questions consistency with camelCase usage.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
nit: Why do we `?` on vertex on some places only?
We should remove from everywhere, and use an early return if reqired. 

There is no runtime safety now, as even if `vertex?.icon` is safe, `vertex.type` check will fail.
comments.label_reasoning: Inconsistent use of optional chaining (vertex?.icon vs vertex.type) means the code doesn't provide consistent null safety, leading to potential runtime errors.

comments.author: saurabhg772244
comments.body: I'll update to `vertex?.form`. Early return is not possible here. We need to check if form is circle square or rounded. if there is anything else will return icon.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: By early return, I meant return early if vertex is undefined. Then we don't need `?` everywhere.

comments.author: saurabhg772244
comments.body: Ohh this will not work. say someone added form as `xyx` which is not valid. when we do early return we will not return shape as icon.

comments.author: sidharthv96
saurabhg772244
comments.body: Ohh my bad I taught you are taking about form or icon is undefined. Vertex will be always defined. I can remove `?`

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests removal of inconsistent optional chaining and suggests using an early return pattern; also flags a runtime safety issue.
